version.changelog: Create a new OpenClaw agent with any messaging channel (Telegram, Discord, Slack, Feishu, WhatsApp, etc.)

llm.summary: The skill's stated purpose (create a new agent and bind it to a messaging channel) matches its instructions, but it directs edits to a system-wide OpenClaw config and to store many external credentials while declaring no config-path or credential requirements — an inconsistency that could lead to unexpected privilege or secret handling.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the instructions: creating a new agent and wiring a messaging account requires creating a workspace and adding channel credentials. However, the skill metadata declares no required config paths or credentials, yet the instructions explicitly read/write /root/.openclaw/openclaw.json and create /root/.openclaw/workspace-groups/{agent}. This mismatch between declared requirements and actual actions is noteworthy.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md tells the agent to create directories under /root/.openclaw/, create multiple identity/workspace files, and to directly read and modify /root/.openclaw/openclaw.json to add agents, channel accounts, and bindings. It also instructs placing service credentials (bot tokens, app secrets, service-account paths) into that config and restarting the gateway. These are within the claimed feature but involve system-wide configuration and sensitive secrets — operations with real security impact.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec or bundled code; nothing is written to disk by an installer. Risk comes from the runtime instructions that modify system files, not from an installer.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables in metadata but expects the user to provide many external credentials (Telegram/Discord/Slack tokens, Feishu app secret, Google service-account JSON paths, possibly phone links for WhatsApp/Signal). Those secrets are appropriate for the task, but the metadata omission and the instruction to store them in a system config file without guidance on encryption/permissions is concerning. The skill also references absolute root paths, implying elevated filesystem access.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill directs modification of a global OpenClaw configuration file (agents list, channel accounts, and bindings). That changes system-wide agent routing and credentials — i.e., other agents or the gateway behavior — which is more than creating a purely local, ephemeral agent. Although 'always' is false, modifying global config is a high-impact action and should be treated cautiously.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill's purpose is plausible, but it asks you to edit system config and store channel credentials in /root/.openclaw/openclaw.json even though the metadata doesn't declare those config paths or secrets. Before using it: (1) only proceed if you trust the skill author; (2) make a backup of /root/.openclaw/openclaw.json and the workspace directory; (3) prefer creating limited-scope tokens for bots (least privilege) and avoid putting long-lived root-level secrets in plaintext where possible; (4) verify file permissions and ownership after changes; (5) consider performing the edits manually (or reviewing the exact JSON diffs) rather than allowing an automated step to modify the global config; (6) confirm the agent runs under an account with appropriate privileges (not unexpectedly root); (7) ask the maintainer to update registry metadata to declare required config paths and expected credentials so the risk surface is explicit.
